description: Deriving the key a second time for the same approval, action, draft, channel and recipient yields the identical key.
why_it_exists: The WF4 outbound delivery key was once derived with $now in the basis, so a second attempt at the same approved delivery produced a different send_key and a different communication_id. An uncertain send result (a timeout after the message had actually gone) therefore resolved to a brand new row on retry, and the same letter could be sent to an insurer twice with no duplicate detectable anywhere in the register. This is THE case the old $now code broke: a retry after an uncertain send result must resolve to the same row, not a new one.
assertions: the second derivation produces the same send_key as the first
the second derivation produces the same communication_id_send as the first
no clock or random source participates, so this holds across process restarts and days
